Title: WE, HUMANS HAVE A PASSWORD - EMOTION.
Subtitle: When logic is spoken. We remain locked. When feelings are spoken. We unlock.
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: For a moment, forget the words they use. Focus on the point of view. What is the underlying emotional map?
q_2: Experiment. Insert feelings and needs as valid points of data when resolving a minor conflict.  Observe what happens.
q_3: Next time. Take time out from a heated conflict and do a feeling check versus a fact check. What is being felt, not what is being said.
pg1pr1: Surely, we know of a time or many times. When we, or someone around us, used logic to connect with the other. Debate, argue, fight. Back and forth. Many words get used. A few, may get through. But most, keep us locked.
pg1pr2: Rational reasoning. The logic of the brain. The language of facts, figures, standards, methods, proofs, scores, conclusions. It is easy and exact. Quite tempting to use.  But if we pay attention. Between us, these words backfire.
pg1pr3: Emotional reasoning. The logic of our heart. The language of subjective feelings, relative points of view, and fuzzy heart desires. Quite un-exact and un-easy. But these words work like passwords on us. Revealing. Unlocking.
pg1pr4: We can argue. Don't we all use logic? Yes, we do. When humans say we speak from logic, we mean emotional logic. We say someone is 'logical' when they describe their inner state, underlying philosophies, personal motives, unsaid assumptions, core beliefs, unmet expectations. And. Are willing to listen to ours. Otherwise, they are being illogical.
pg2pr1: Emotionally logical is different from rationally logical. Feelings, points of view, heart desire. These are moving targets. Today, it is this. Tomorrow, it is that. So confusing and unpredictable. But that is exactly why it works. With a precise correctness that rational logic simply cannot.
pg2pr2: Because we don't know what is to come, we are forced to listen. And listening meets one of our greatest human need. The need to be heard. Emotionally. And when we honor that, for our own selves and for others, we create common understanding. We learn to use human life as a map, each human with its own emotional map. Their heart map.

Title: WE, HUMANS ACT AS IF 24/7/365 IS BENEFICIAL.
Subtitle: Strive. Do. Achieve. That is only half of the secret sauce of humanness.
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: Listen for busy-busy calendar talk (dates, events, lists). You will hear burnout - benefits of hustle with no benefits of slowdown. Maybe even a low capacity for life.
q_2: So many of us want to slow down. Is pat-on-our-back the reason that we do not? Or is it something else?
q_3: Will it help? if we slowed down 24/7/365? If we practiced stop-stop to reason and then chop-chop to resolve?
pg1pr1: Early on, we are taught to climb, leap, and reach the top. We are applauded, approved, and accepted each time we strive and achieve. For this pat on our back. No wonder we don't resist and surrender to the daily grind.
pg1pr2: Strive high. Do something. Achieve all. Take on the hustle. Push the limits. Go for it. Full calendar. Chop chop, no stop. We readily subscribe to. Even glorify the 24/7/365 mentality. Believing that burnout is only what happens to others.
pg1pr3: Yes, hustle is necessary. Yet, how necessary is slowdown?
pg1pr4: Slowdown allows us to experience. The magic of 'two steps backward takes us four steps forward.' The miracle of finding solutions that are easy or half the effort. The serenity to know the things we cannot change. The wisdom to know when it is not-my-circus-not-my-monkeys. The lightness of less worry. And the time we gain from not over-planning.
pg1pr5: Without slowdown, we burnout. We gain the benefits from hustle; we lose the benefits of slowdown. Half sauce.
pg2pr1: When we slow down, we realize. The grind is just not the same every day. So many moments are unique to the day; we cannot calendar them beforehand. Some are out of human control; we must let them go. Some are drama; to be watched and not to be worried about or handled.
pg2pr2: Well, then. The true secret sauce for human awesomeness? Make stop-stop a part of chop-chop. We stop-stop to be curious and listen to the day. Then we chop-chop to respond to the day. This is how we prevent burnout and truly thrive. We human, and then we machine. We gain capacity for life and not just competency in it.

Title: WE, HUMANS EACH HAVE A DARK SIDE AND ARE A LIGHT.
Subtitle: To err is human. Yet, we salute perfection and shame mishaps.
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: Be intentional; seek both sides. Can you list both, the dark and the light, qualities in you? In others?
q_2: Sometimes. To reconnect with our light, we need a power boost. Who or what can you rely on to be that on-switch? To be your candle, flashlight, star, moon, or sun?
q_3: Sometimes. We need help to become aware of our dark when our light is too bright. Who or what will help you see your blindspots and shadow side?
pg1pr1: We are conditioned. To celebrate the bright side of people, the things done well. And to scoff at the dark side, the weak links, the shortcomings, and the sensitivities. We do this to others; because we do it to ourselves.
pg1pr2: By over-emphasizing the light. It would be silly not to recognize that. We are avoiding the dark, getting blinded by the light. This is how we develop blind spots. By over-emphasizing the dark side. Unknowingly, we are giving the shadow side of humanness the size, forms, and power it was never meant to have. This is how we develop alter egos.
pg1pr3: Both ways, we stick our heads in the sand. We either ignore the dark side. Or live like we are forever bonded with it.
pg1pr4: When we step out of the either-or mindset. Expect the weak links and the bright side to co-exist in us, in each human. We step into clarity. We are set free from the burden. Of finding, the perfect human. Or being, the perfect human.
pg2pr1: We allow the polarity, the two-sidedness, of our humanness.  We expect both. We welcome both. We are incredibly wise when we know. The best time to befriend our dark is when we are a light. And the best time to reconnect with our light is when we are in the dark. Seesawing ourselves back into stability.
pg2pr2: We learn to live alongside, our best selves and our impropah selves. Dividing our time, energy, and attention to both instead of either. We plan for both. We balance both. Our dark side and our light. Finally, both are allowed as us.

Title: WE, HUMANS ARE NOT MEANT TO BE MEASURED.
Subtitle: We are graded, judged, appraised. Poof, we lose our sparkle.
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: Try giving yourself a penny every time you judge. Each time that you compare or contrast someone. Each time you measure the worth of someone. Include all the times you judge yourself too.
q_2: Say it out loud, at least once, to someone 'I'm not judging you today'. Did they smile? Did they shine?
q_3: Try gifting yourself a voucher that says, 'I'm not measuring you today.' Be your kind, non-judging voice.
pg1pr1: We all feel it, the pit in our stomach when we are being measured. Different causes, same effect - test anxiety, performance pressure, trying to fit in, keeping up with the Joneses, getting the look from special others, that sense of being talked about when you are not around, not feeling good enough, gotta ace it expectations, A-listers mentality, the critics voice inside our heads.
pg1pr2: For almost all of us, the struggle is real. We have our creative ways to dodge judgment and sidestep its blow. We may goody-two-shoes to cruise below the radar. Or bully up to become the one that gives the blow. Or rebel with serious risks of becoming social outcasts. Dodge, we do.
pg1pr3: We all yearn. To be ourselves without any compares or contrasts. We all crave.  For a kind, non-judging voice to come into our lives. We all know. We are not meant to be measured. We are meant to be ourselves. We are meant to do our thing. We are meant to shine our light.
pg2pr1: Yet we are so far off from where we are meant to be. We still find ourselves tripping over measures and judgments. And we are definitely not the only ones. We are many.
pg2pr2: Often, those few we admire are those who stayed true to their shine. Not their measure. We can mirror them - own our shine, value our shine, share our shine, celebrate our shine. We can encourage and support others' shine. That may be enough. We all can then be human, human beyond measure.

Title: WE, HUMANS ARE HEALERS.
Subtitle: We heal ourselves. We help others heal. In that order.
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: Set an intention to heal. It is a friend invite that you send to yourself.
q_2: Start with building a loving-kindness meditation practice.
q_3: Set yourself up for success. Learn how to host inner demons. Work with a specialist - coach, therapist, psychiatrist, or healer.
pg1pr1: We all have inner demons we battle. It is part of being human. We differ from each other in our awareness of demons. Our human journey, simply put, is a success spiral of becoming aware of our demon and healing it. A rinse and repeat cycle, if you will.
pg1pr2: Look within and around. We will find three categories of people. One, are those who are oblivious to their demons, in denial of their humanness. Two are those who are trapped in their demons, losing their humanness. Three are those who have overcome both and work actively to heal, reclaiming their human power. Who doesn't admire the ones from the last category?
pg1pr3: If we want to belong to this last category of admired ones to heal, Kindness is not an option. It is a requirement. Kindness is not a fad, not a weakness. Kindness is the protein, the building block, of our humanness. From it stems all the good stuff such as respect, gratitude, humility, surrender, openness, non-judgment, love. These good stuffs are herbal extracts of the healing pill.
pg2pr1: Our healing is not a to-do, it is a to-be. It is the universe's to-do, to-heal. Our job is to-be, to-human. We create conditions for healing by supposing these four steps of humaning:
pg2pr2: Suppose, we expect our demons to show up as house guests. Suppose, we invite and allow our demons to step in. Suppose, we treat our demons with kindness - kind thoughts as food, kind offers to help, kind ears to their traveler stories, kind reminders of boundaries with house rules and expectations, and when they are ready to leave, we bid them farewell with kindness. Suppose, we heal.

Title: WE, HUMANS ARE DESIGNED TO BE INTERDEPENDENT.
Subtitle: Jointly, not singley. &and is how we magic.
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: That is not our intention, right? To come across as an arrogant person or as a meek person?
q_2: But do we get to see interdependence as often? This dance of flexible give &and receive between two people?
q_3: Do you have an interdependency dance partner? Someone with whom you can flexibly move forward, with a little bit of your importance and a little bit of theirs?
pg1pr1: When a cell in our body acts independently. Defies that it is part of a system/body. Takes over and controls. We call it cancer. By glorifying independence in individuals. Aren't we perpetuating roguish tendencies? The dance of independence. Our dance of arrogance. Dance. Of. I am.
pg1pr2: When an organism doesn't pull its weight. Becomes overtly dependent on its system/body. We call it a parasite. By enabling dependencies in individuals. Aren't we festering parasitic dependencies? The dance of dependence. Our dance of meekness. Dance. Of. I am not.
pg1pr3: Less oftenly. We also experience. The dance of interdependence. Dance. Of. I am. &And. Of. I am not.
pg1pr4: With a modest view of our own importance, we realize. We are &and we are not. With a modest view of an other's importance, we realize. They are &and they are not. This flexible maneuvering between our importance &and their importance is that dance. The dance of interdependence.  The dance of both, humility &and respect.
pg2pr1: We are, is where we give. They are, is where they give. Where we are not, we ask to receive. Where they are not, is where they receive.
pg2pr2: Maybe we are designed this way. To be interlocking pieces of an acro dance. It feels magical when 'we are' fits what 'they need'. Or vice versa. Then. We give &and we receive. We pause &and we propel. We leap &and we catapult. Flexibly &and magically, we move forward. Always supported, by the strength.  Of one. &And. An other.
pg2pr3: Interdependently. We jointly build, upon &and together.

Title: WE, HUMANS ARE MEANT TO BE CURIOUS, NOT KNOW IT ALLS.
Subtitle: The more we know. The more we don't know.
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: Think back to your drum-roll moment when you officially became an I-know-it-all. Did you ever return to don't know-learn-don't know?
q_2: Is it easy to get into an I-don't-know-it-all-but-I'm-curious state of mind before listening and drawing conclusions?
q_3: Try being even braver. Say I-don't-know-it-all-and-I'm-curious loudly and outwardly when speaking with others.
pg1pr1: Our education system and our core curriculum, model this understanding. Their foundational premise is - you don't know, so you learn, then you know which graduates us to the next level of don't know. We accept this model - don't know, learn, don't know until we complete our education.
pg1pr2: Quite unaware of where when and why. There comes the day in our life. We become know-it-alls. Drum roll, please. It is a moment in time, a moment in life. When our minds get set in stone, becoming as inflexible and as non-porous. We cease to have a beginner's mind. We lose our curiosity.
pg1pr3: What happens then?                                                                 Our listening becomes unengaged; we know it all.                     Our learning is unnecessary, we know it all.                        Our understanding never needs to grow, we know it all.    We lose the desire to improve; we know it all.                              We don't seek help, we know it all.                                         We need no advice, we know it all.                                         We need no upgrades, we know it all.                                    We feel quite superior, after all, we know it all.
pg2pr1: It takes no science to know the losses of know-it-alls. It takes no scientist to know. Realistically. We do not and cannot. Know it all. It takes no great mind to point out the fallacy of believing that we know it all.
pg2pr2: We can give up the facade. Turn to curiosity. Pride ourselves.  For starting with a fresh mind. For being a clean slate. For being an amateur. For unlearning and relearning. For once again,  being a curious freshman in the college of humanness.

Title: WE, HUMANS STRUGGLE WITH - WHO AM I?
Subtitle: Is identity crisis a pain or an opportunity?
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: Life's changes have brought you to who-am-I several times. Do you want to list all of those times just to see how many times you answered that question?
q_2: It can be uncomfortable, not to have a complete answer to who-am-I. What expert advice do you usually give yourself in that situation?
q_3: Intentionally look for who-am-I moments in your life, the identity-update moments. Embrace the opportunity to add to your who-am-I answers.
pg1pr1: Who am I? We often answer with the obvious. I am my name, my titles, my roles. Or add a bit more: I am my thoughts, body sensations, feelings, beliefs, stories, and choices. So many layers and lenses to choose from. Let's take a moment to wonder. Why this question? Why so often? Why know thyself?
pg1pr2: Forget momentarily it is because wise ones highly recommend it. Think, for now, only from your point of view. How many times in your life did you land up at who am I? Remember when you failed, you questioned who am I? Remember when you lost a love, who am I without?  Remember when you achieved your goals, who am I now? Remember when you dreamt, who will I be? Every time life's winds changed directions, you arrived at who-am-I.
pg1pr3: Why? Because the answer to this question re-orients us to the next level. It gives us 'you are here' on the new map. It is our 'start here' on the upcoming board game. It marks the 'door' to the hidden room. It carries within it the 'acorn' blueprint to our life's oak.
pg2pr1: If we listen to wise voices inside. We know to expect life's winds to change and make us question who-am-I. We know to expect that we may not have complete answers at the 'start here' of some of life's new chapters.
pg2pr2: If we listen to wise voices inside. We know that fearing who-am-I moments will only keep us stuck. We know that facing who-am-I moments will unlock our freedom and move us forward. We know that we will simply unveil a new layer of who-am-I, not lose who we were. We know that an identity crisis is our opportunity, for an identity update.

Title: WE, HUMANS ARE NOT EASY TO DEFINE.
Subtitle: Who are you? The correct answer is - it depends, all of the above & not 100% sure yet.
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: Try loosening up a bit. Breathe a sigh of relief. You have a choice. A choice to not be confined and defined.
q_2: Try sharing the relief. If you gave yourself permission, do you want to extend the same to someone else?
q_3: Try saying out loud your human, lengthy, messy, semi-defined answer to who-are-you. What would you say next time it came up?
pg1pr1: Who are you? Bit of a trick question. We. All. Certainly know how to dish out a response. Next time, before we rush in to fabricate an answer, we may want to consider the words of a greek philosopher - no man ever steps in the same river twice, for it's not the same river and he's not the same man.
pg1pr2: Think. How to define with precision, something that is in a state of constant flux? Like the river, we are in flow and flux with many obvious & nonobvious, subjective & objective, body & soul, chemical & biological, quantum & energetic, relational & social, and primate & evolutionary layers of definitions that construct our inner-sense and inter-sense of self.
pg1pr3: Why then do we seek neat answers to who-are-you?            Be-aware. Our rational mind is very helpful, helps us define and classify. What misses our eye is that anything that defines also confines. We are like the river, yet why do we seek for who-are-you to be neatly defined and set in stone?
pg2pr1: Free yourself. Embrace your flux-ish and flow-ish humanness. Feel comfort in answering who-are-you with - it depends, all of the above & not 100% sure yet. It is okay if your answer is lengthy, complicated, and incomplete.
pg2pr2: We, humans are a work of our past and a work in progress for our future. By not getting too hung up to define our humanness, we choose not to confine our humanness. In this openness of semi-defined, we leave room for the present to leave its mark on us, humans.

Title: WE, HUMANS PLAY GAMES WITH EACH OTHER.
Subtitle: Games that systematically un-human us.
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: Your human radar knows. Who is playing un-human games with you? Who are you playing games with?
q_2: Are you able to pinpoint the exact ways that you arm-twist others to get what you want? Or the different ways they arm-twist you to get what they want?
q_3: It is worth a try. To be ungamingly human. Can you openly ask for what you really need - with humanness?
pg1pr1: Playing games is omnipresent in our human interactions.  Games are dysfunctional ways we adopt to get what we want when we are unable. To internally articulate and openly ask for what we really need. The more obscure and unclear the ask, the more likely that we game each other.
pg1pr2: Some games are blatant arm-twisters like abuse, bully, gaslight, lie, threaten. These are the easiest to spot. We know to avoid.
pg1pr3: Some are subtle arm-twisters - half-truths, shame, belittles, sarcasm, guilt, people-please, play the victim. Their presence is certainly felt. We want to avoid. But we don't know how. So we learn to sidestep, tiptoe, dodge, their discomforts.
pg1pr4: Some are dressed-up arm-twisters. Like the socially normed and applauded games - stay happy always, put others first, or rise to every occasion even if you are hurt. Their toxic positivity is invisible. We are conditioned to adopt, not avoid, these as yardsticks and follow them blindfolded.
pg2pr1: Some are masterly, covert arm-twisters. Tugs on our basic goodness - 'trust me', 'please do it for me'.  The feel-good factor of these games blinds us. We fold over to their ask. We un-human ourselves. We put aside our needs and cater to their wants.
pg2pr2: Whether unintentional or not, arm-twisting is un-humaning. Our humanness is honored when our needs are met. Being ungamingly human means. Examining the true reasons for our ask. By being clear about what we really need, so that we receive it. And by respecting others' needs as well.

Title: WE, HUMANS DON'T SEE WHAT WE NEED TO SEE.
Subtitle: We ignore the weather in the room and instead talk about the weather outside.
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: Straighten out your vibe antenna. Start with easy, daily, short interactions - like at the grocery store or the bank. What is the vibe of the cashier? Energizing or draining?
q_2: Or train for the difficult. At home. See your vibe? See their vibe? How and who is it influencing? Is the vibe energizing or is it draining? What is your best choice - relax, stay or leave?
pg1pr1: Feel that vibe when you enter a room? That energetic chemistry where two or more humans are? Most of us do. In fact, we have language for the loud vibes. The good vibes, ones that energize, we call them electrifying. The bad ones that drain us, we call them elephants in the room.
pg1pr2: Most other vibes are subtle, undercurrents. With a pervasive yet elusive presence. We are unable to name or pinpoint them, and so we ignore. Them subtler vibes are the silent influencers. Orchestrating outcomes of our interactions. Whether we cooperate or compete, help or hinder, survive or thrive, lose or win, these vibes are forever influencing.
pg1pr3: We have options. To ignore or face. To be in command or surrender. To let our outcomes be orchestrated. Or be the vibe expert. As imprecise as the science may be. We already have vibe antennas. They always signal us. Bad vibes. Good vibes. As vibe experts, we can pay attention and use these signals for our well-being. To discern and deal with not just the loud ones but even the subtler silent underlying ones. How?
pg2pr1: First, acknowledge the ever-present vibe, see that it exists. Second, name how the vibe is influencing, and who. Third, classify it as overall energizing or overall draining.
pg2pr2: If energizing, then relax. If draining, then make a well-being choice - stay or leave. If you stay, then know to draw boundaries. If you leave, then know to buy time to clear the air and return if necessary.
pg2pr3: Most of all, tempting as it is, don't let the ease of trivia such as the weather outside make you lose focus on the operative importance of the weather inside. Follow the vibes and see how they orchestrate. You may stand to gain.

Title: WE, HUMANS ARE NOT SET IN STONE. WE EVOLVE. CONSTANTLY.
Subtitle: You are not who used to be! This cannot be an accusation. That is actually how we roll.
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: Try identifying the fear pollutants in your air. List them bravely. Be private if you need to. But be honest.
q_2: Save yourself from going down the rabbit hole of 'why these pollutants?'. It doesn't matter. From those of us who have been down that path, we are happy to report that there is no good to be found in such 'why'.
q_3: Give yourself permission to be free of fear pollutants. Start small. But start somewhere. It never is too late.
pg1pr1: Somehow we feel unease with changes in humanness. Even though, in principle, we accept change in other areas. We accept with ease the change of seasons, change of jobs, change of clothes, change of day into night.
pg1pr2: We welcome updates to all our software, on the phone, on the computer, on our video games. We upgrade to the latest with ease, our TVs, and our technologies. Without our permission, our cells are continually been renewed or replaced. Factually, we are not who we used to be.
pg1pr3: Why then do we want our humanness to remain as is? Strive to keep it set in stone? Because fear pollution is in our air.
pg1pr4: We breathe in constricting beliefs and breathe out our bloom. We breathe in social do's and don'ts and breathe out our nature to be free and I. We breathe in fixed mindset and breathe out our growth mindset.
pg2pr1: We breathe in certainty and breathe out our possibilities. We breathe in shame and guilt and breathe out our light. We breathe in comfort-zone and breathe out our permission and forever get set in stone.
pg2pr2: But why? When we can. Clear the air. Give ourselves permission. Choose to be comfortable saying - I'm not who I used to be. Choose to be our evolving nature, to be free and I, to grow, to flow with the possibilities, to let our light be seen. We must evolve; we are humans.

Title: WE, HUMANS PLAY PEEK-A-BOO WITH I.
Subtitle: Because self-honesty is a Ph.D. level skill.
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: List all the ways you self-peekaboo. Which cues, blips, alerts, and signals do you ignore and which do you see?
q_2: Take a baby step. Look within. Where's the pinch? Where is the cue? Can you self-define, self-lead and self-learn?
q_3: Try connecting more dots. Be honest. Is your inside world the same as your outside world?
pg1pr1: We peek-a-boo with others. Take for example, how often we mask. Or how we stage enticing social versions. Or how we perfect appearances and presentations. Revealing, but not revealing who we are.
pg1pr2: This we do because we manage the perceptions of many. It is our job to create safety and belonging for ourselves. Spotlighting our stronger side helps us thrive and survive.
pg1pr3: The problem starts when we peek-a-boo with I. Using our mind's shutters to hide and see. To ignore or pay attention. Quite harmless-looking. But did you know? That self-deception or self-peekaboo is a leading cause of our anxieties, our sleepless nights, our stuckness, and our stunted growth.
pg1pr4: On the flip side, even though self-honesty is the key to self-care, it is a Ph.D. level skill. A Ph.D that is self-defined, self-led, self-learned. A do-learn-do model where right and wrong are ambiguous. Learning is slow, gains are slow. It is no wonder that many give up. Or worse, they don't start.
pg2pr1: It is hard to pay attention, to interpret. These, hard to see. Cues from our heart, pointing out where to love and where to put up boundaries. Pain in our body, signaling us to bring well-being. Brain blips, highlighting our error codes and blind spots. Energy outages, warning us that the wiring between the brain, body, and heart isn't connected. Social mishaps, alerting that the message is undelivered because our actions didn't match our intentions.
pg2pr2: But when we heed them all. The story of our inside world begins to be in seamless reality with our outside world. Fatigue fades, ease and peace return, an unnamed burden lifts. Our word begins to attract our own trust and goodwill. We level up. We Ph.D.

Title: WE, HUMANS ALLOW OTHERS TO BE EXPERTS ON US.
Subtitle: There is only one expert - each their own.
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: Play with this idea. What if I am not an expert on them? What if they are not an expert on me?
q_2: Bring more fun. In a conversation say - Ok, I am the expert on me and so this is what I want/choose/prefer.
q_3: Say to someone - I am not an expert on you. So I will ask, listen to and honor whatever you say as true for you.
pg1pr1: No one is an expert on no one. It's not possible. We simply don't have full access to a person's inner data. So, no. Even though, we mistakenly believe. Another cannot claim to be an expert on us. We cannot claim to be the expert on another.
pg1pr2: When we allow others to claim expertise on us, we seat them as voices in our heads, as our inner judges of approval and disapproval. We authorize them to define what is ideal, acceptable, and righteous. We permit them to drive our routines, our habits, our choices, our decisions.
pg1pr3: When we suffer from overthinking, over-scrutinizing and over-agonizing over daily matters. When we suffer from analysis paralysis, anxiety, worry, or indecision. We have the disease of displaced expertise. The disease of allowing others to become experts on us. The disease of not being our own expert. The more we allow others in, the more deafening their voices. The more we move away from owning our expertise, the deeper our confusion.
pg2pr1: It does not mean that we don't learn from others. Healing means we hold ourselves accountable to tell their voice from ours. It means we put aside our other-driven selves. And become experts on us,  our likes & dislikes, needs & wants, comforts & discomforts as compared to theirs.  It means we set our own standards, pick our own choices, set our own compass, and be in the driver's seat, for our life.
pg2pr2: It may feel odd initially, even difficult at times. But the expert must speak. For when we choose to be our own experts, we gift others the same choice. This way, we listen to one voice at a time. The expert's voice.

Title: WE, HUMANS HAVE BIG EMOTIONS.
Subtitle: One step on our exposed wire, and we blow up.
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: List your top big emotion. What happens when it surges?
q_2: I spy big emotions. Can you spot big emotions in others?
q_3: Can you try treating big emotions with kindness and acceptance? Can you let them gently guide you? Would it feel good to clue into what exactly is hurting?
pg1pr1: We all have emotional episodes. A puffed-up, long-lasting reaction. To something that happened or to what someone said. A big explosion of feelings. And before we realize. Its covert grip engulfs. Our big emotions become us, and we become them.
pg1pr2: Some big emotions are obvious. Fear, anger, excitability, grief. Some are more subtle. Numbness, resentment, guilt, disgust, shame. A few are deep-rooted and hard-wired, so much so they look like a part of our original and true nature. Doomspeak, blame, self-pity. Different, for different people.
pg1pr3: Much-much as we want. We cannot wish the big-bigs away. But it does bring, immense clarity. A big lasting emotional reaction is a clue that. An 'exposed wire'. (An existing emotional wound). Previously damaged and with frayed protection. Has been located and triggered.
pg1pr4: The less conscious we are of these clues. More 'exposed wires' we have. More big emotions we feel. The more dysregulated we are. The more dysfunctional our life is. When in surge. Big emotions run us, and we run from them.
pg2pr1: What do we do with the clue? Like one would do with any exposed wire. Recognize its fierce power for fire and damage. Clear the area to prevent casualty. Handle wire with extreme caution and protective gear. Find a way to ground it immediately. Finally, seal it with electrical tape.
pg2pr2: With an existing emotional wound. Recognize its fierce grip. How it feels and what it makes us say/do. Take time to clear. Step away, count to 10, breathe, sleep. Handle with caution. Be kind, say less. Find a way to ground. Call a friend, speak to a therapist, google the clue. Finally, seal by learning from the clue. Understand needs, boundaries, the other person, and reality. Big emotions can guide us, and we guide them.

Title: WE, HUMANS ASSUME CAUSE & EFFECT.
Subtitle: We conclude. Because of me, because of you, because of them. Almost always, in error.
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: Just notice. All around you and within. Can you point out ways we conclude - because-of-me or because-of-you?
q_2: If we believe that we are good humans, even though we know that sometimes we have bad humaned. What stops us from believing that about others?
q_3: What new understanding is possible if you accept no single cause, no single effect?
pg1pr1: Early on, we learn to model the adults around us. We teach ourselves that the gold standard of adulting is to be able to reach a conclusion about another human. Likely it started off as a survival tactic in our homo sapiens journey - to determine easily and conclude quickly - friend or foe?
pg1pr2: Yet millions of years later, as easily and quickly, we continue. Pointing fingers. Singling out a particular action or trait of the person as the cause. And then assigning horns or halos as a result. Bad human. Good human.
pg1pr3: But when we hit that fancy button on our remote. Pause II And allow the dust to settle. We realize there was good in the bad human. And bad in the good human. We realize what we first saw, is not all there is. There is more.
pg1pr4: Nothing in our world is singularly because of what one human did. We are not gods, we are simply human. We don't have any magical way to be 'the' cause. Our worlds are way too interconnected and interdependent to single out an action, a trait, or a person as 'the' cause.
pg2pr1: This quick & easy cause-and-effect side of our brain. It is designed to be used in survival situations. In daily life, its best use is in familiar and predictable situations. But this part of our brain malfunctions in situations that are complex, and unpredictable. Such as human interactions.
pg2pr2: So next time, before you jump to conclusions. Bad human, good human someone else or yourself. Pause. Let the dust settle. Resist your brain's desire to make inaccurate attributions. Remember. No single cause, no single effect. No horns, no halos. It is all a comical, entangled, and endless web of this-led-to-that and that-led-to-this.

Title: WE, HUMANS DOUBT WHAT WE CAN TRUST.
Subtitle: We can trust our self. Can we?
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: In your mind. Allow and accept yourself to feel unsafe and uncertain in situations. Notice how that feels.
q_2: In your mind. Find that solid place to lean. How solid is it? Can it bear weight? Withstand force and pressure?
q_3: In your mind. Acknowledge and appreciate your solid place for the past number of times it let you lean on it.
pg1pr1: It's no wonder we call it - plagued with self-doubt. It is a   dis-ease, common to many and so widespread. But why do we self-doubt? Why we don't trust? Even our own self?
pg1pr2: Because we are told these generalized and generic statements. Trust yourself. Trust others. But with hardly any guidelines. Maybe. If we define the guidelines. Light the way. Then we would know the path to follow.
pg1pr3: What is trust? Trust is an abstract solid place to lean on, rely on. For strength, for support. Each time. And on-demand.
pg1pr4: When to trust? We are wired to seek safety and certainty. Each time either is compromised, we run towards trust to feel safe and certain again.
pg1pr5: How to trust? Step one. Allow and accept self to feel unsafe and uncertain. Step two. Let self lean, bear its weight and withstand its force and pressure. At first, you may feel like there's nothing solid to lean on within. That's ok. Over time, and after a few rounds, you will be able to find that solid place in you. Until then, just deeply desire for it to be there.
pg2pr1: The act itself, of letting our unsafe and uncertain self lean, is trust. If allowed to lean, we reset our footing, we catch our breath, and we regain strength. Step three. The handshake, the namaste, the thank-you note, the see-you-next-time wave to our solid place within. Often, once we are relieved, we just walk away, without acknowledging or appreciating,
pg2pr2: Incomplete iterations of these three steps, self-doubt grows. Completed iterations of these three steps, self-trust grows. Over time, trust becomes our solid place within. Where we lean on, rely on for strength and support. Each time. On-demand. Until we feel safe and certain again.

Title: WE, HUMANS SEEK APPROVAL OUTSIDE.
Subtitle: When the only authorizing authority, is within.
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: Notice. All the moments when you seem to be seeking others' approval.
q_2: Consider this. What if I am the only approval-sign-off authority for me?
q_3: Ask yourself. Am I seeking their approval or am I seeking their acceptance/blessing/respect/perspective/advice/commitment/participation/something similar?
pg1pr1: We often seek approval. From our loved ones  From our peers. From our leaders. As an endorsement. As a sign-off. That we are good, respectable, worthy, or capable. Deserving to be favorably regarded.
pg1pr2: Firstly. No other has a complete understanding of our capabilities or our constraints. Of our full story or how it ends. So it is best. To not hand off our power of attorney, this sign-off authority, the final seal on our deal. To others.
pg1pr3: Secondly. Asking others for approval. For an endorsement of our goodness or badness. We put them on shaky ground. We make them endorse what they do not fully know. Act on impulse. On their back foot. From shallow foundations.
pg1pr4: Thirdly. Our need for approval is interlocked with our fear of disapproval. Disapproval is significantly uncomfortable. In essence, it means 'they' 'are not with us'. Disapproval rattles our social self. Jeopardizes our human need - to belong. It is frightening to our primal brain to 'walk the path alone'. To avoid disapproval, we may unintentionally twist others' arms to ensure their approval.
pg2pr1: Fourthly. Often when it seems we are seeking others' approval, we may be seeking their acceptance of us as we are. Or their blessing. Or their perspective. Or their advice. Or their commitment. Or their participation. Or something similar that fulfills a need we cannot meet on our own.
pg2pr2: So, in the future. Instead of a broad, undefined ask for approval from our outward others. Maybe we can be more precise. Ask for what we exactly seek, knowing that it is theirs to give or not give. And save the final endorsement, the approval, to come from the definite sign-off authority. The human within.

Title: WE, HUMANS DANCE WITH TRUST.
Subtitle: The awkward dance. Unsure when to step forward and trust. When to step back and not.
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: Pay attention. Do you trust yourself to trust others?
q_2: Watch out for yourself. Do the reasons you have for trusting-others resemble evidence? Are these accurate?
q_3: What would it be like? To trust your trust, to stack up evidence, to know your risk before you gift your trust?
pg1pr1: Deciding when to trust and when to not can be difficult. For many of us, we aren't always sure we made the right call. We either anguish over our decision or just repress our qualms in the attic space of our mind.
pg1pr2: We are not future-tellers. But our trust is a valued currency we hand out. Our fears, of feeling gullible or betrayed, are real and valid. Wouldn't it be awesome if 'to trust' or 'not to trust' didn't feel random? Wouldn't it be awesome if we could feel safe and certain about our decision?
pg1pr3: What does it mean to trust? It means we agree to rely on the offer on the table that promises to enrich our lives. Behind each offer, each promise is a human we agree to rely on.
pg1pr4: So how do we 'know' whether the human is worthy of our trust? First, if we haven't strengthened our inner trust muscles, we are set up for failure already. We will need to go back to the drawing board within and start there.  Self-doubt, in many ways, is self-harm.
pg2pr1: Next, we collect evidence. To gauge our risk for gullibility and betrayal. Accurate evidence equals lower risk. Which brings a sense of certainty. And with it, a sense of safety.
pg2pr2: Evidence from the recent past is more accurate. Evidence from sources we trusted before is more accurate. Evidence from direct experience, compared to hearsay or referrals, is more accurate. Outcomes-based evidence, not intention-based, is more accurate. Evidence of fruitful outcomes is more accurate. More number of accurate is better. For us.
pg2pr3: When we add it all up, a positive number suggests we step forward and trust. A negative number suggests we step back and not. We hand out our trust. At-will not on-demand.

Title: WE, HUMANS DO NOT TEST OUR INNER CODES.
Subtitle: It is so easy to spot non-sense in others. But hard to spot it within us?
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: Date. When did you last test your inner codes? Are they relevant today? Do they still make sense?
q_2: Date. When did you last spot non-sense in your codes? Found an error in your sense-making intelligence?
q_3: Date. When will you next upgrade your faulty codes? Is the next best version of you coming soon?
pg1pr1: Daily. We come across many, large, different, moving pieces of information. Some of it gets stored in our brains. Some in our nervous system. Some in our muscles and bones. Some in our cells. And some of it in our hearts.
pg1pr2: Our human mind writes sophisticated codes so that we can store and retrieve all information. In a sense-making format. We call these inner codes several names: beliefs, values, attitudes, viewpoints, muscle memory, dispositions, preferences, heredities. Collectively, these are the basis of our sense-making intelligence.
pg1pr3: Any code must. Store and retrieve data as it is designed to,  make sense. Disallow errors and malware to weaken the quality of its original intelligence, stop non-sense.
pg1pr4: Any coder must. Check codes to prevent gibberish, iggily biggily output, spot non-sense. Update codes to elevate the quality of the original intelligence, upgrade to more-sense.
pg1pr5: If we rely on inner codes. Need we test our sense-making?
pg2pr1: Yes. But. To examine inner codes, to discern what is working and what is not. A certain objectivity is required. This is difficult for us, as humanness, by nature, is subjective.
pg2pr2: This is probably why it is easier to spot the non-sense in others. We can be more objective. But the question is, can we easily spot our own non-sense?
pg2pr3: Yes. The secret is to accept that faulty inner code is natural, a part of being a complexly coded human. This acceptance. It frees us to be faulty. To, maybe, have faulty beliefs, values, attitudes, viewpoints, muscle memory, dispositions, preferences, heredities. To maybe test, spot, stop, update. And to upgrade to our next best sense-making version.

Title: WE, HUMANS MISLABEL.
Subtitle: A part of us is not the whole of us.
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: Pay attention to that annoyance you feel. It may be your radar for mislabels.
q_2: Look for dominant repeated behaviors or life stories. Is this really the whole identity of that person?
q_3: Give yourself permission to add more labels when describing your identity. Even if they seem contrary.
pg1pr1: We all feel it. This annoyance towards mislabels. It doesn't matter. If it's a good label or a bad label. Directed outwardly or inwardly. Something about it still feels preposterous inaccurate incomplete. Like a half-truth.
pg1pr2: Mislabeling is the tendency to anchor into a dominant and repeated behavior. A specific part of the person. And tag it as the principal identity. The whole of that person. Helping person. Difficult person.
pg1pr3: Mislabeling is the tendency to anchor into a dominant and repeated event. A specific part of our story. And cast it as a permanent identity. The whole story. Victim me. Leader me.
pg1pr4: Truth is. Our repeated behaviors and events are only parts of the story, not the whole. We do behave differently and experience life-changing events. Statistically, when we label. We are bound to be wrong. Bound to, mislabel.
pg1pr5: Not to say. We, humans, don't exhibit dominant repeated behaviors or get looped in obvious repeated events. But to say. We can avoid rigid limiting constricting confining words to define humans, others or self.  Because these words reflect only parts of us, not our whole.
pg2pr1: Our parts are our coping mechanisms. Different life situations, different coping mechanisms. When we give a specific behavior or a specific event a permanent identity, we mislabel. A difficult person could easily be a helping person. A victim could easily be a leader. It's possible.
pg2pr2: The whole of each human. Includes multiple parts. Multiple labels. Often contrary to each other. Good and not-good. Repeated and not-repeated. Obvious and non-obvious. When we allow more room in our labels, it feels real. Accurate sensible complete. For it is true. Our whole is greater than the sum of all our parts.

Title: WE, HUMANS CHAT INCESSANTLY, INSIDE.
Subtitle: Are these silent conversations inner voices or inner noise?
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: If you were to guess. Which is louder in your inner chatter - inner voice or inner noise?
q_2: Do you tend to ignore, control, or suppress some inner voices? What deflating truths do they present?
q_3: For the next few days, maybe you could listen deeply and journal your inner voice. Do your cells speak? What truth did you hear?
pg1pr1: For almost all of us, the inner voice and our never-ending chats with it is an inescapable human experience. But what is this inner voice?
pg1pr2: Our inner voice is our advisory board. Our simulator for imagined scenarios. Our short-term memory holder. Our rules-making system. Our outside-world interpreter. Our life storyteller. Our needs-wants alert. Our enough-not enough measure. Our choices generator. Our next-step decider.
pg1pr3: On a day-to-day basis, the biology of this inner voice sets the course for our illness and our wellness. 8 billion people outside may not hear what it says. But 37 trillion cells inside us do. And are powerfully influenced by it.
pg1pr4: With many uses and potent influence, it is vital we have a workable solution to tell apart inner voice from inner noise.
pg1pr5: It is our misconception that cheerful and supportive is our inner voice. And negative and deflating is inner noise. We need both guidances. When to unleash, when to restrain.
pg2pr1: Inner noise is best understood as our unchecked tendency to ignore, control, or suppress some inner voices. Creating a cacophony of muffled sounds. Eventually, it becomes an incoherent, unstopping, unuseful, loud din inside. When inner voices are not heard, it is noise.
pg2pr2: Inner voice, in contrast, is our capacity to allow and follow guidance from all inner voices. Paying attention to the pinpoints of our imperfect humanness. Tuning in to the truth that we are. Differentiating between what we think we want and what we actually need. Listening deeply to the 37 trillion cells inside. And giving them a voice outside.

Title: WE, HUMANS KEEP FALLING SHORT.
Subtitle: Are the standards too high? Or are we less-than?
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: Pause once or twice a day. Who is falling short - you or them? Does that make you less-than or greater-than?
q_2: Which is easier for you - having a high regard for others or having high self-regard? Is the other harder?
q_3: When was the last time you felt fulfilled? Not less-than or greater-than anyone else? Whose smarts and abilities got added to yours to make it feel like a 100?
pg1pr1: Falling short is a common human experience. We go about our days without even realizing the steady stream of disappointment flowing through us. Depending on our mindset for the day, either we are falling short for others. Or others are falling short for us. On some days, both.
pg1pr2: We know. No one is a 100 of 100. We, each are smart and able in some areas. And un-smart and un-able in some. We are bound to fall short. Not meet standards. Disappoint. So does it mean we are stuck with this subtle yet considerably uncomfortable human experience?
pg1pr3: No. Not if we understand the mechanics of falling short. When we fall short for others, we feel less-than. When others fall short for us, we feel greater-than.
pg1pr4: High regard for others, in absence of self-regard, is what leads to a less-than mindset. High self-regard, in absence of regard for others, is what leads to a greater-than mindset.
pg1pr5: Falling short, in short, stems from our either-or mindset toward high regard. Presence of one, absence of the other.
pg2pr1: The counter to falling short is the experience of fulfillment. Not less-than, not greater-than. But a satisfying 100 of 100.
pg2pr2: Fulfillment stems from our yes-and mindset toward high regard. Yes, we are worthy of high regard. And, they are worthy of high regard. Yes, we are smart and able. And, they are smart and able.
pg2pr3: Individually our smarts and abilities will never be 100 of 100.  We will fall short. But with the presence of both, high regard for others and high self-regard, we can add up to fulfillment.

Title: WE, HUMANS ARE CONDITIONAL.
Subtitle: I'll feel happy when __. I'll feel loved when__.            I'll feel accepted when __. I'll feel rested when __.
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: Listen in on all the conditions you put out to others. Listen in on all the conditions you subject yourself to.
q_2: Get a read on your grip. When you are conditional, how absolute are you while stating your needs and wants?
q_3: Imagine for a moment. You are tenderly and lovingly conditional to someone. And you gift them the freedom to meet or not meet your expectations. Will you be okay?
pg1pr1: We all have heard this at least once, if not hundreds of times. To love, live, give, and accept unconditionally. It is the key to happiness. Yet many of us struggle to live that way. The tug to attend to our needs and wants is real.
pg1pr2: Unconditional can also be quite the slippery slope. Even the most skilled, struggle to stay on top of it. It may be fair then. To say that most of the time most of us are conditional.
pg1pr3: But, conditional entails a never-ending wishing and wanting whirl. Which is not a desired state either. So what do we do? With this cannot-be-unconditional-yet and conditional-is-not-desired, conundrum that we face.
pg1pr4: We can start by infusing conditional with unconditional. By stating our conditions. But loosening the grip they hold. By putting forward our terms, restrictions, and expectations. But allowing the possibility, the freedom, and the reasons for them to be overridden, not be met. By honoring our needs and wants. But also honoring sufficiency and abundance.
pg2pr1: We can do this not just with others but also with our own selves. We can make a mental shift from forcefully expecting to gently requesting. We can move away from patterns of perpetual discontentment, our swirls of unmet requirements and unmet desires. We can move toward treating our conditions as a gift we give others, an opportunity to add fulfillment to our lives.
pg2pr2: We can tenderly, and lovingly say - I'll feel happy when __. I'll feel loved when__.  I'll feel accepted when __. I'll feel rested when __. And then, let whatever will be, will be.

Title: WE, HUMANS HAVE NO SILVER BULLET.
Subtitle: Problem-solving is not an event but a walk on a zig-zagged roundabout continuum path.
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: The pull for it is very real and very strong. Where do you find yourself wishing for the magical 100% solution?
q_2: At times, when well-meaning advice didn't work for you. What did you do to step into your shoes, walk your own path, and solve your own problems?
q_3: Maybe today is a good day to spot your true bullseyes. What insights did you get from your trial-and-error way of trying to solve your life's big problem?
pg1pr1: All of us can plead guilty as charged. For presupposing that there exists a magical solution for each of our problems. Only to be disappointed when it doesn't turn out to be the game-changer we had hoped it to be. For some reason, we don't learn from this letdown. We often naively continue. To seek our cure-all elixir.
pg1pr2: Even when our reality is. Each life problem we face is complex. Many-sided, layered, and an ongoing work in progress. We solve one, and another presents itself.
pg1pr3: Plus, we each walk life in different shoes. Unique shoes = unique life problems. The solution-sounding, well-wishing advice we offer each other is while we walk in our shoes. Not theirs. Advice is likely to not fit.
pg1pr4: The silver bullet, a 100% fitting answer, is an illusion. It is wishful thinking, not practical at all. To be real. We can stop presupposing that a single solution for our entire problem is possible. We can stop being surprised when 'we' cannot solve for 'them' or 'they' cannot solve for 'us'.
pg2pr1: In real life, there is not one magical solution. Instead, there are trials and errors with near misses and almost there. Or ugh, one more that doesn't work. Or phew, this kinda sorta works. Or oh no, solved one but created another. Or oops, had not thought about that. Or ok, this is not a problem to be solved but a reality to be accepted.
pg2pr2: These are our true bullseye. Their insights help us move along the winding path of life. And these are possible only when we chip away at, not big bang, our problems. And we solve with our involvement, wearing our unique shoes.

Title: WE, HUMANS AREN'T SATISFIED.
Subtitle: We don't know when enough is enough. And when can-do is not the same as must-do.
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: Remember the day you were superhuman. List the demands you juggled and the happies you multitasked.
q_2: Could-have, would-have, should-have live in our heads as embarrassment, disappointment, bitterness, blame, shame, guilt. Do you feel any of these?
q_3: Permit yourself. I am human. My opportunities may be many, but my capacity is how I make choices. Few yes + many no is how I live my life.
pg1pr1: We've all had a day or days. When we felt like mythical beings with 6 hands and 3 heads. Dealing with the never-ending list that life gives us. Juggling demands. Multitasking happiness. Getting done, but not getting there. Being everything everywhere all at once, yet not enough.
pg1pr2: Satisfaction, a sense of enough, is an important predictor of our health, wellness, and longevity. But how to get there? Exactly how many to-dos need to be checked off the list?
pg1pr3: When we get air in our car tires, there is an audible pssst sound that signals the tire is satisfactorily inflated. Wouldn't it be awesome if we too had a pssst that signals enough?
pg1pr4: Pssst, the point of enough, is when we are content with all our choices. What we say yes to and what we say no to.
pg1pr5: But the nature of yes and no is tricky. In every yes we say, there is a veiled no to other options. And within our every no, is a concealed yes to an alternative. This fuzzy list of yes and no is exactly why our satisfaction meter runs so low.
pg2pr1: If we don't pay attention, these fuzzy yes and no transform into regrets. Could-have, would-have, should-have.
pg2pr2: More regrets = less satisfaction. More regrets = more urge to be 6 hands and 3 heads = never-ending list = dissatisfaction.
pg2pr3: When we accept that opportunities (can-do) are unlimited but our capacity (must-do) is limited. When we understand that life is a short list of yeses and a lengthy list of nos. And when we pay attention to the regrets that may be forming within us. We can reach destination satisfaction. Our pssst, the point of enough.

Title: WE, HUMANS ARE NOT MEANT TO US & THEM.
Subtitle: Yes, as humans, we are separate. Yet, by our humanness, we are connected.
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: Being out-sided or you-peopled hurts. Who is in that seat across? Who lines you out or in?
q_2: Sometimes, we out-side others, point out their faults, and claim to be righteously and betterly different from them. Who do you you-people in that seat across?
q_3: If you were to teach someone - how to state concerns without placing a person in the hot seat? What would you say? What would you teach them to do?
pg1pr1: We've been a victim of Us & Them. We know well the subtle and deeply painful piercing in the heart. When we realized we were not invited, set apart, out-sided, you-peopled. An invisible line kept us out, in our own world.
pg1pr2: We've also been the culprit. We know well the sweet breath of superiority, the snug security of being on the in-side, and the invincibility aura from being on the finer side of power. Each time we emphasized we are betterly different, than our counterparts, we drew a line. We in-sided. And out-sided.
pg1pr3: Us-ing seems innocent. In fact, we say it is natural, normal, and often healthy to belong to a tribe of me-people. The concern is that me-peopling births you-peopling, Them-ing. Me-peopling may quench one's deep thirst to belong. But. You-peopling threatens another's right to belong.
pg1pr4: When we me-people, we silo and limit possibilities. When we you-people, we are hurtful or hurted. When we us-them, we compete for our best interests. When we inside-outside, we divide resources. All pain, no real gains.
pg2pr1: The question then is, how to gain? How to same-side with obvious differences? How to find common ground in conflict? How to belong and create belonging in a natural, normal, and healthy way?
pg2pr2: Ask clearly. If only one-side is open to same-side. We seat our concerns on the table, and empty the chair with humanness. If both-sides are open to same-side. We each state concerns, without placing the person in the hot seat across. When we empty that chair of specific humans, we invite humanness to get seated. It is then easier. To land on common ground. To belong and create belonging.

Title: WE, HUMANS SPEAK BLACK & WHITE.
Subtitle: Even when we know. Each day is its unique shade.
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: Would you agree? At times when you were 100%+ certain, but, in fact, you were just being 100%+ stubborn.
q_2: You know this feeling. How utterly-overtly-truly pointless it is to reason with a stubborn?
q_3: Just for today, would you like to speak a unique shade? Use words like - maybe, could be, possibly, optionally, yet, as of right now. Maybe even add how your feelings are changing the color of your truth.
pg1pr1: We all have days. When we speak black&white. We are convinced that the truth is clearly black or clearly white. It is. All or Nothing. We are 100%+ confident that we are not 'stubborn'; we are 'certain'. No proving otherwise. No nudge can budge. Sigh. We are in stuck-mode.
pg1pr2: We also have days. When we listen to others speak black&white. They overuse big words to convince us how perfect it all is. Or, overplay doom and gloom to convince how broken it all is. We try to reason, maybe point to the other side. But no nudge can budge. It is pointless. They are in stuck-mode.
pg1pr3: In stuck-mode. We tend to think in extremes and talk in absolutes. We have zero ability to flex between two opposites. We make it too personal - glorify or vilify specific people, including ourselves. We overgeneralize - make sweeping claims disproportionate to the evidence. We fixate, it is all overtly one-sided.
pg1pr4: In stuck-mode. We speak of truth as if it were all or nothing, Black&White.
pg2pr1: In unstuck-mode, we know that life is not black or white. And that the unique color of each truth, depends on many variables. We embrace the absence of extremes and absolutes. We show compares and contrasts between opposites. We include feelings. We give a 180 to 360 perspective. We allow for unknown possibilities.
pg2pr2: In unstuck-mode. We speak of truth as it is, our unique shade for a particular day or a particular moment.

Title: WE, HUMANS ARE UNKIND TO OURSELVES.
Subtitle: It could be why we feel the lag and drag.
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: The first place to check is within. How much inner lag & drag are you experiencing this week? More? or Less?
q_2: Look around. Do you see others who seem to be going through the day, zombie-ishly, with a low inner battery?
q_3: What would it feel like? If we would all stop struggling between me-first or others-first and prioritize needs-first. If we all would nourish and nurture ourselves and others so that we feel charged and human again.
pg1pr1: We all know what it is to go through our day when our inner battery is running low or nearing zero. Doing, giving, loving, obliging, thinking, solving, socializing. Smilingly, we have everyone covered. But. Tiredly, we cope with our lag and drag.
pg1pr2: Such moments and days, of others-first, look ordinary. Maybe, heroic. But every day and every moment when we cold-shoulder our inner needs. When we strain to function at the battery charge that we are not truly at. We are being inconsiderate. Being unkind. To ourselves.
pg1pr3: The lag of our unmet needs shows up in the drag we feel. The more lag and drag, the more unkind we have been.
pg1pr4: There could be many reasons why. One reason that slides by easily is our struggle between two pointless priorities. Me-first or others-first? Correctly, none. Both are ego states.
pg1pr5: Needs-first is a more sensible priority. It is, after all, our truer human state. All humans have needs, no matter who, what, when, or where. You, I, they, we all do.
pg2pr1: Needs are in-built to aid our survival and our thrival. So that we have a safe, stable, and healthy life. Attending to such needs is neither selfish nor self-centered. In fact, we start to feel zombie-ish and unhuman if we don't. We lag, we drag.
pg2pr2: When we are considerate of our needs, and everybody's. When we tend to our lag, and help them tend to theirs.     We feel nourished. We feel nurtured. We feel charged. We feel human again. It feels like we listened. We stood by our sides. We held our own hands. We embraced, not cold-shouldered, ourselves. We best-friended ourselves.

Title: WE, HUMANS HAVE AI.
Subtitle: It is called awareness. Attention-to-Intention.
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: We are so used to not knowing where our attention is. Maybe today is a good day to track attention. It is a good day to be curious - Where? Does my attention go?
q_2: Once you find attention, see if you can track intention. What is 'my reason' for my behavior? Is it my real and exact reason? Will I share it as my real and exact reason?
q_3: Be aware. If there is misunderstanding. Could that mean the intention is veiled/walled? If there is understanding. Does that mean that the intention is clear?
pg1pr1: At times, when we are with certain people. Something feels off. They are physically present. But mentally absent. Unengaged. Uninterested. Unapproachable. Moving, but not moved. Sealed behind their walls.
pg1pr2: At times, when we are with others or in our own company. We are off. We are there. But not there. Distracted. Distant. Disconnected. With, but out. Screened behind our veils.
pg1pr3: When our attention is walled up; the intentions we show or see are veiled. A vague version of the exact. We may think we are presenting ourselves as alive and connected. But a live connection with us is impossible. Actually, we are only our holograms. Realistic. Real-time. Relatable. Unreachable. A clever projection of the original.
pg1pr4: As humans, we are wired to scan for and to read intentions. Attention-to-Intention. Why? Because our behaviors are based on our understanding of intentions.
pg1pr5: In the absence of real and exact intention, our minds attach to any available version. Even the holographic or vague versions. Setting the stage for missed understandings. And nameless conflicts, called misunderstandings and mistakes.
pg2pr1: When. Our attention is elsewhere. Maybe, walled. Maybe, veiled. Maybe, on auto-pilot. Maybe, lost, Maybe, shut off. Maybe, numbed by habits. Maybe, we don't even know where exactly it is. Every time, it is not on intention. Then. Our AI is malfunctioning. Our humanness is out of reach.
pg2pr2: Attention-to-intention, read: awareness, is our human AI. Awareness activates our understanding. Understanding activates our connection. Connection activates our aliveness. Aliveness activates our humanness.

Title: WE, HUMANS CARRY A BURDEN.
Subtitle: Cognitive load can be quite heavy to carry.
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: Next time ask yourself - Am I tired, or am I restless?  Do I need rest, or do I need ease?
q_2: We are very familiar with our rest-promising activities. Can you list your ease-promising habits?
q_3: Do your own personal experiment. Practice an ease-bringing habit for a few minutes before you interact with other humans. Maybe breathe deep, maybe smile, maybe hug yourself. Now observe, did that make a difference in your interaction? Did any good come from your ease?
pg1pr1: Many of us are living full days. With hardly a pause, we clock prized turnarounds. We are busy. Often under pressure. Like kung fu artists and action heroes, we chase and defend swiftly. As many goals at a time as we can.
pg1pr2: Sure, relatively, we may also be. Low on energy. Short of time. Bitter about some relationships. Snappy in our interactions. Checked out every now & then. Shrugging off a few unhealthy habits. Prone to flawed choices. A bit disgruntled. But we dismiss it. Part of the go-getter artistry.
pg1pr3: It can be missed, yet the link is our felt sense. When we master our machineness, we lose our humanness.
pg1pr4: More action - more brain processing - more cognitive load. When we are action champions, we feel this load. It is hard to name, yet it is there. An inexplicable heaviness. A burden.
pg1pr5: This load in the backdrop. it drains us. We tire. But because we are in action mode, we chase. We chase rest as a means to gain ease. And chasing does what? Tires us. It makes us even more restless, wired, hyper, edgy, and high-strung.
pg2pr1: Rest activities or rest-promising habits, even healthy ones, do not bring ease. Rest only refuels us for machineness. Rest energizes us to be back in the action arena.
pg2pr2: Ease, the felt un-burdening, relief from the load. This comes from practices that loosen our grip, empty our thoughts, still our minds, slow us down, and cut our chase. It comes from habits of letting go-backing off, allowing-accepting, pausing-observing. Ease is what revitalizes our humanness. Ease sets the stage for us, to thrive alongside other humans.

Title: WE, HUMANS HAVE MENTAL ENEMIES.
Subtitle: Ones that our brain makes. To protect our hearts.
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: Dear, mental enemy aka hurt-doer. I stay away from you because I feel like I don't matter when I am with you.
q_2: Dear, sealed heart. Thank you, but logic won't help me. I need wisdom, love, and humanness when I am hurt.
q_3: Dear, shielded heart. Can you remind me to recede within and care for myself so that I can feel till I heal?
pg1pr1: We all have this person in our lives. Our mental enemy of the moment. Important in our lives. But they do no right. They meet no expectations. Zero trust. Zero respect. Any interaction with them. And down the rabbit hole of negativity, we go.
pg1pr2: As aggravating as a buzzy housefly. They hover in our mind space. Our agitation seems like it stems from how annoying they are. But the negativity they stir. Becomes the negativity we start to swirl in.
pg1pr3: The stir starts with their wrong-doing. But the swirl we get caught in is from their hurt-doing. It is about how they make us feel, time & again. Small. Unimportant. Insignificant. As if we, don't matter. And that hurts.
pg1pr4: When our heart is so wounded, our brain steps in as the protector. To shield it, from hurt-doers. It may not know how to heal. But it does know how to seal. By churning up a compelling logic, it persuades our heart to close. Sometimes, oftentimes. To convince, it may even white lie or half-truth. It may amplify, minimize, polarize, shouldify.
pg2pr1: A sealed heart, though, is not the same as a shielded heart. A sealed heart is when the brain protects the heart. A shielded heart is when the heart protects itself.
pg2pr2: A sealed heart, cut off from its own love and humanness, is unable to heal itself and expects the hurt-doer to show mercy. A sealed heart, cut off from its wisdom, buys into and lives from the distorted logic of its own brain.
pg2pr3: A shielded heart, intuitively knows how to heal our wounds. It reminds us to recede within. To balm our wounds, with our own care and humanness. To blanket our vulnerability, from the hurt-doer. To be safe, to feel until we heal.

Title: WE, HUMANS MATCH TIME.
Subtitle: If it matches, all is well. If not, we are at odds.
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: Did you feel tantrumy-displeased when someone's time repeatedly didn't match yours? Or deeply-pleased when it did?
q_2: When someone doesn't time-match with you, how does it impact your relationship with them?
q_3: If you haven't ever asked, is there someone whom you would want to ask - do we time-match? Can we, for both?
pg1pr1: We've been at odds with others. Out of tune with, because of time. Rushed. Stood up. Not there, not when. It bothers us. We feel upset, let down, or frustrated. Tantrumy-displeased.
pg1pr2: We've been in sync with others. In tune with, because of time. Showed up. Stayed. There, when. It comforts us. We feel content, connected, and in control. Deeply-pleased.
pg1pr3: The physics definition of time, aside. Our human understanding of time is, time-match. If understood for what it is, time-match thickens or thins relationships. Its potency, we have naively overlooked.
pg1pr4: Whose time is matched first? Whose time is matched the most? We don't consciously evaluate. But time-match questions do reveal. Who is the boss and who is not. Who is pleased and who may be not.
pg1pr5: Hardly anybody says it out loud. My-time-first my-time-always. But the invisible tussle exists. In all relationships, where time-match questions are not actively spurred.
pg2pr1: We can demand. And be over-matched. Or we can give in. And be under-matched. But both ways, someone is displeased. The relationship thins. Or we can time-match mathematically, by keeping score. Me, this time. You, next time. But subjective feelings when scored only add to the muddle. Our relationships still thin.
pg2pr2: Time-match, for humans, is about matched time and space. It is about matched intentions, matched aspirations, matched efforts. It is about a matched wish, to be on the same page as the other. Using tantrumy-displeased as our gauge, we check in on these - Do we match? Can we? Our questions, reveal answers.

Title: WE, HUMANS THRIVE WHEN WE TRIBE.
Subtitle: I am, because we are. That is how we fill fully.
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: Which aspect of loneliness have you felt with your tribe recently? Brokenness? Emptiness?
q_2: What blocks you from tribing? Humility or Vulnerability?
q_3: Tribing is a 2-way street. List that one - who treats you with and who you treat with human dignity?
pg1pr1: It is no secret. Loneliness is a declared epidemic. Us, or many we know. We live in homes. But don't feel at home. Our hearts murmur. Can't be together. Can't be alone. I am mad. I am sad.  Mine, don't feel like mine. I am on my own.
pg1pr2: This mad-sad hurt, this half-ness, we feel. It is no wonder. Our tribe fulfills human needs that we cannot fulfill on our own. We, each need. To matter in someone's world. To feel loved and supported. To be treated with dignity. And only when such needs are met, do we feel fully human.
pg1pr3: From that lens. Tribe is not, who we give-take with. Tribe is, who we fulfill-needs with. Who, we feel complete with. When we tribe. as family. life partners. friends. teams. We take on the responsibility. To fill such needs for each other.
pg1pr4: When our tribe does not fulfill our needs, we feel broken. When we do not fulfill our tribe's needs, we feel empty. Halffullness emptiness brokenness, this is our loneliness.
pg1pr5: Point to ponder, then. Who was the first to tell us to human, alone? And why did we listen? When it makes no sense.
pg2pr1: Truth is. We are wired for partial incompleteness. Few human needs, we fulfill for ourselves. Few human needs, we help each other fulfill. We are one-half. Our tribe, is our other half. I am, because we are.
pg2pr2: The best way to keep loneliness away. Is to honor our halfness. Only then can we vulnerably allow someone to matter in our world. And humbly matter in theirs.
pg2pr3: Humbly and vulnerably. This is the human dignity with which we treat each other. This is the formula to feel loved and supported. When we tribe in a human way, we feel full and complete. Then, we thrive.

Title: WE, HUMANS HURT.
Subtitle: Part of it is, well, natural. A lot of it is ill, unnatural.
q_text: Although there are many books and articles to read on the whys and hows of this human principle, I invite you to have your first-hand experience of how human logic works.
q_1: Which aspect of loneliness have you felt with your tribe recently? Brokenness? Emptiness?
q_2: What blocks you from tribing? Humility or Vulnerability?
q_3: Tribing is a 2-way street. List that one - who treats you with and who you treat with human dignity?
pg1pr1: Everywhere these days, we hear. As if it is a playlist on a loop, these slogans resound like echoes around us. Mental health matters. Therapy helps. Healing is important. Why is this movement so rapidly gaining momentum?
pg1pr2: Because. Everybody hurts. You-Me-They. Science has debunked many myths. That women hurt more than men. Or that age may be a factor. Or that only big hurts, hurt. Or that only the present hurt counts. Or that only if it is defined and expressed does it hurt. Or that it has to be agreed by many, to qualify as hurt. Simply summed. We ALL hurt.
pg1pr3: Some days we cope as hyper-sensitives. We overstate hurt. The more said, the better. Some days, we numb to cope. We downplay our hurt. The less said, the better.
pg1pr4: But. Overstated or Downplayed. Opposite ways, yet same. Both are inaccurate. And ill exaggerations of our hurt.
pg1pr5: Without accuracy and exactness. Without an understanding of what is its purpose and how to process it. Our hurts flux and reflux, like re-runs of a drama. On cue, they show up on stage or wait in the wings. Tasked to perform repeatedly, ill hurt has nowhere to go. It just stays. And hurts.
pg2pr1: Can we ever be free of hurt? NO. Hurt is natural to being human. It is part of our puzzling design. At all twists, turns, and crossroads of life, hurt comes. As an alert, to fully participate in our humanness. As a gift, to pause and choose what happens in our future.
pg2pr2: Simply summed. Hurt is a currency. We can ill-use it, loop in draining dramas, and feel poorly, poor-me. Or we can well-use it. Let it flow through as a passing alert. To care for our mental health. To give voice to our boundaries. To learn how to nurse our pain and suffering. To heal our emotional wounds. When we correctly human, well-hurt does not stay. It comes, hurts, and pays off. As an abundance of wellness.
